title: Customer ops minutes and friendly status notes — replay-first draft
body:
Purpose:
A friendly, concise status update and post-incident customer summary draft intended for: (1) status page short messages, (2) a follow-up postmortem for affected tenants, and (3) self-serve verification and replay steps customers can take. This is a working draft — primary goals: clarity, actionable guidance, and limits on technical noise.

Key principles for this draft:
- Start with one-sentence impact and apology.
- Offer clear customer actions (how to verify, how to request replay/evidence).
- Include a short timeline and high-level cause; avoid internal-only signal words.
- Commit to next steps and when customers will see a finalized postmortem.
- Provide contact + escalation path and SLA/credit guidance.

Suggested short statuspage snippets (select one per update window):
1) "Resolved: We observed a regional inference queue delay affecting select requests in eu-west-1 between 2026-01-14 02:12–02:52 UTC. Root cause: throttling storm caused by a routing change. No customer data loss. Follow-up postmortem will be published week of 2026-01-25."
2) "Partial recovery in progress: routing fixes deployed — most requests are serving normally; a small fraction of long-tail requests may still experience retries. If you see repeated failures, try switching region or contact support for replay evidence."
3) "Under investigation: reduced throughput in eu-west-1 causing elevated latency and occasional timeouts. We are actively mitigating and will update within 60 minutes."

Customer-facing post-incident summary (concise):
Impact summary:
- Time window: 2026-01-14 02:12–02:52 UTC (peak effects 02:20–02:35 UTC).
- Affected surface: hosted inference endpoints and streaming sessions routed through eu-west-1.
- Severity: elevated latency and occasional request timeouts for ~6% of tenant traffic in region.
- Data integrity: no data loss; payloads and logs retained for verification.

What happened (short, non-technical):
A routing change combined with an unexpected traffic spike which triggered an aggressive autoscaling governor in the eu-west-1 fleet. This caused a transient backlog and some requests were retried or timed out. We removed the faulty routing rule and tuned the autoscaler to prevent the governor from engaging on short bursts.

Timeline (customer-facing granularity):
- 02:10 UTC — small routing config was rolled (internal canary).
- 02:12 UTC — customers begin to see elevated latencies as routing overlapped with a traffic burst.
- 02:18 UTC — alerting triggered; SREs start mitigation.
- 02:22 UTC — partial rollback of routing change and temporary override to autoscaler policies.
- 02:30 UTC — majority of traffic serving at normal latency.
- 02:52 UTC — full mitigation confirmed; we began normal rollforward and verification checks.

Immediate customer actions (self-serve verification & replay):
- Check your request logs for 2026-01-14 02:10–03:00 UTC. Look for 429/504 status codes and record request IDs.
- If you need deterministic replay, open a support ticket and include example request IDs; we will run a replay and provide outcomes + raw evidence for each replayed request.
- If you host with Dedicated or Private, consider pinning to a region or model variant temporarily — see guidance link below.

Support & evidence options we are offering:
- Replay kit: upon request, we will re-run stored requests against the recovered fleet and provide per-request logs and model outputs (available for affected customers for 30 days).
- Audit package: for enterprise customers we can provide SHA'd request payloads, routing traces, and timeline artifacts.
- SLA/credit: if your SLO was breached, submit a claim referencing "INFRA-4583" in the ticket. Our support team will validate and respond within 5 business days.

What we changed (preliminary fixes):
- Reverted the routing rule that created overlapping routes for a small shard of tenant traffic.
- Temporarily widened autoscaler thresholds for short burst resilience and reduced the governor sensitivity.
- Added a short-term traffic watchdog that prevents simultaneous fast roll changes + autoscaler adjustments.

Planned long-term mitigations (high level):
- Better preflight checks for rolling routing configs (safety gates + dry-run telemetry).
- Autoscaler policy refactor to decouple short-burst detection from capacity-capping logic.
- Enhanced customer-visible incident telemetry on the status page (per-region percent impacted).
- Postmortem and follow-up RFC to be published in Confluence by 2026-01-25 with engineering-level details and timeline.

FAQ / quick answers:
Q: Were my data or prompts exposed?
A: No. There is no evidence of data leakage or corruption. All request payloads were logged and retained for replay verification.

Q: Do I need to change my integration?
A: No general change required. If you have strict latency SLAs, consider regional pinning or a multi-region routing policy; contact your CSM for help.

Q: How do I request a replay or evidence?
A: Open a support ticket with request IDs and tenant ID. We created a template ticket tag: "replay-request-INFRA-4583" to help prioritize.

Draft customer email / status update template (concise):
Subject: Brief update — regional inference delay in eu-west-1 (Jan 14)
Body:
Hi — we wanted to update you quickly: between 02:12–02:52 UTC on Jan 14 we saw elevated latency and intermittent timeouts affecting a subset of requests in eu-west-1. The issue was due to a routing change interacting poorly with autoscaling thresholds; we reverted the change and applied mitigations. No data loss. If you observed errors, please share request IDs and we will run a replay and provide outputs + logs. A fuller postmortem will be published by Jan 25.
Thank you for your patience — Maya (Customer Reliability)

Open questions / engineering asks (internal notes for draft conversation):
- Can SRE provide the definitive tenant impact CSV (tenant, request-count, error-count) for inclusion in the enterprise audit package? (ask by 2026-01-20)
- Product to confirm whether we should proactively offer replay to all tenants that saw >=1 timeout or wait for inbound requests.
- Legal: verify wording around SLA credit process and acceptance window.

Next steps for this doc:
- Iterate with SRE and product to add the tenant impact table.
- Finalize the customer-facing timeline (engineering review) and lock message for statuspage.
- Publish versioned postmortem on Confluence (target 2026-01-25) and link from statuspage.

Owner & escalation:
- Draft owner: Maya Gonzalez (customer-success). Escalation path: Customer Success -> SRE on-call (pager) -> Eng on-call -> Exec on-call.

Notes to comms writer (tone):
- Keep sentences short, avoid deep infra jargon, emphasize no data loss and available replay/evidence.
- Use bulleted actionable items for customers.

---- end of draft ----
